name: Central Kalimantan
summary_text: Central Kalimantan is listed in the dossier among the provinces with no sub-national signal: no enacted discriminatory bylaw, raid, arrest or incident series targeting transgender people was found, and the province is NOT one of the eight identified in OutRight International's Creeping Criminalisation analysis of discriminatory regional regulations (that list covers Aceh, DKI Jakarta, East Kalimantan, Lampung, North Sumatra, South Sulawesi, South Sumatra and Yogyakarta). For a visitor, Central Kalimantan therefore tracks the national baseline: the KUHP criminal code in force from 1 January 2026 criminalises same-sex conduct nationwide, and ordinary Sumatran/Java-style local moral policing is absent here — but there is no province-specific enforcement record in either direction. Any risk follows the country's national framework rather than a local divergence.

sources.claim_summary: OutRight Action International, 'Creeping Criminalisation' (Katjasungkana & Wieringa, 2022): mapping of national laws and regional regulations violating rights of women and LGBTIQ people in Indonesia; its eight-province list of discriminatory regional regulations does NOT include Central Kalimantan, which is the basis for treating the earlier 'one of the eight provinces' attribution for this unit as a misplacement of East Kalimantan.
